headline: Binance loses ~$6.3B in a hack, $1.57B liquidated; short-term buyers turn to loss selling with price just 1.8% above their cost basis.
summary: The Binance hot-wallet theft set off $1.57B of liquidations; STH-SOPR fell below 1 to 0.9917 and short-term realized losses rose 95% in a week, so buyers from 80–82K are now selling at a loss. Weighted funding snapped back from 0.64% to 9.85% in a day while the Coinbase premium 7-day average fell further to −0.174%: leverage is back, US spot demand is not. Bull day 22, no exit rule triggered; watch whether closes hold the 75,819 short-term cost basis.

overview.lead: An exchange theft pushed price down to the short-term holder cost basis and underwater new buyers began selling at a loss; leveraged longs rebuilt immediately while US spot kept selling at a discount.
points: Today's finding: STH-SOPR 0.9917 (Oct 30) is the first reading below 1 since Aug 14; broken down, realized losses rose 95.4% in a week while realized profit fell 35.6% (CheckOnChain).
About $6.3B was stolen from Binance's hot wallet with ~$3B frozen; 24-hour liquidations hit $1.57B (CoinDesk, Oct 30). BTC's intraday low was 76,155.
Weighted funding 0.64% → 9.85%; Coinbase premium −0.243% on the day (7-day average −0.174%); ETF Oct 29 provisional +$17M.
Bull market day 22, supporting lights 4/6 (exchange-supply light turned on today); no exit rule triggered, nearest action level is the 200-day MA at 73,115 (−5.3%).

cycle.lead: Bull day 22 and supporting lights rose from 3/6 to 4/6, but price is only 1.8% above the short-term holder cost basis, the closest of this bull phase.
points: 51 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA (73,115; 71,264 thirty days ago); bull market since 2026-10-09.

On (4): MVRV vs its 1-year mean (1.447 > 1.418), realized cap 30-day +0.91%, exchange supply 90-day −0.18% (on today), close above the short-term holder cost basis 75,819 (Oct 24). Off: 12-month momentum −29.0%, STH cost basis 4.81% below True Market Mean (Oct 24).

At the last 30 days' pace the STH cost basis crosses True Market Mean around 2026-12-17; with price flat, 12-month momentum turns positive around 2027-02-01. Both are linear extrapolation / flat-price assumptions, not forecasts.
Tidemark (Oct 30): top signal 0, bottom 23.4; cycle-low test in progress: no break of 58,525 before Dec 19.

news.title: Binance hot wallet hacked for about $6.3B; ~$3B frozen, deposits and withdrawals paused; TRM Labs attributes it to North Korea's TraderTraitor
news.read: Possibly the largest exchange theft ever; co-CEO Yi He said Binance will cover all losses. Stolen assets were mainly stablecoins and Ethereum-ecosystem tokens (frozen funds include $2.3B of stablecoins); BTC was dragged down by risk aversion. Our exchange supply 7-day change swung from +0.31% to −0.62% (Oct 29), which may include the hacked wallet's outflows, so it should not be read as hoarding. An industry shock that does not change the market stage; watch for run-style exchange outflows once withdrawals resume.

news.title: $1.57B liquidated in 24 hours, $522M in BTC; BTC briefly fell to 76,400, its lowest since Sep 18
news.read: The second large long flush in two days. Yet our weighted funding jumped from 0.64% to 9.85% in a day, and the article notes BTC funding positive and rising: longs came back after being flushed, so the next drop still has liquidations to amplify it. Short-term structure; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: Nasdaq down about 3.4% near the close, Intel down nearly 30%; 10-year yield fell to 4.90% and December hike odds dropped from near 90% to about 70%
news.read: AI-spending worries hit tech for a second day and BTC followed (30-day correlation with the Nasdaq 0.66, FRED Oct 29). Lower yields and hike odds would normally help, but risk aversion dominated both days; our real yield of 2.63% (Oct 29) is down 30bp over 20 sessions, one of the few improving backdrops. No change to the cycle view.

news.title: FOMC holds rates at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted another quarter-point hike
news.read: A pause after September's hike, but two votes for hiking keep December (Dec 9) live. A tight backdrop for BTC with our real yield still high at 2.63%; price did not react much on the day, and the drop came later from tech and the Binance hack. No change to the cycle view.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs took in $17.07M on Oct 29, a fourth straight day of inflows; Grayscale BTC saw $15.35M of outflows
news.read: Inflows fell about 88% from the prior day, and the data predate the Binance hack; we list it as a provisional value (Farside via CoinDesk matches at $17M). Four days total about $440M, yet the Coinbase premium 7-day average hit a new low at −0.174%: ETF buying is not offsetting US spot selling. Flows backdrop; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25% (8–1), confirms underlying inflation has met its 2% target for the first time; markets expect a December hike
news.read: Japan is in a hiking cycle and a shrinking yen carry trade is a medium-term global liquidity headwind, but this hold was expected and did not trigger a sharp yen rally. Background for BTC; no change to the cycle view.

news.title: The hacker borrowed about $44.6M of ETH on Aave against stolen USDT; Aave briefly froze lending markets on 16 networks, then reopened
news.read: The spillover was mostly in Ethereum DeFi (Uniswap and Aave tokens fell about 11% in a day), and USDT and USDC are temporarily barred as collateral for new loans. For BTC it is indirect risk sentiment with no direct trace in on-chain BTC data; our stablecoin supply is down 1.17% over 7 days, so watch whether freezes accelerate the decline.

news.title: Tether reports $1.5B Q3 net operating profit, excess reserves up to $7.95B, USDT supply about $184B
news.read: A thicker reserve buffer at the largest stablecoin lowers the risk that the theft becomes a stablecoin confidence crisis. But total USD stablecoins are down $6.6B over 30 days on our data, so sideline money is still leaving; no change to the cycle view.

findings.title: New buyers turn to loss selling; the 75–76K short-term cost basis is the last line
findings.lean_why: Buyers who took over above 80K are selling at a loss with price only 1.8% above their aggregate cost and thin supply down to 66K; but loss depth is still shallow, not capitulation.
findings.what: Question: after losing True Market Mean, will underwater new buyers sell, and where is the next line? STH-SOPR fell from 1.0029 to 0.9917 (CheckOnChain Oct 30), its first reading below 1 since Aug 14; short-term supply in profit 39.8% (bitcoin-data Oct 29; 88.4% a week ago, 7-day change at 1-year percentile 1.1); network net realized P/L −$819M (CoinMetrics Oct 29, 1-year percentile 11.8), with the 7-day sum swinging from +$2.9B to −$230M. Close 77,204, 1.83% above the 75,819 short-term holder cost basis (bitcoin-data Oct 24).
findings.why: Breakdown: which side moved? Short-term realized losses 3,555 BTC (1,820 a week ago, +95.4%) vs realized profit 4,681 BTC (7,274 a week ago, −35.6%): mainly more loss selling, not less profit taking. Cost map (CheckOnChain actual coin age, data date Oct 30): short-term holders 3.657M BTC, average cost 75,064; the densest buckets, 80K (616K) and 82K (518K), are underwater. Two points in time (modeled, Sep 20 → Oct 29): of the 3.622M BTC short-term supply then, 1.151M moved, most from the 80K (328K) and 76K (260K) buckets; 1.660M BTC bought since and still unmoved sit at 80K (714K) and 82K (416K). Model-free part: supply above 88K, a range price has not revisited, fell from 4.054M to 3.800M BTC (−255K), so old coins are selling too; LTH-SOPR 0.838 (bitcoin-data Oct 29) means long-term holders are selling at a loss. Cross-check: funding rose back to 9.85% and the Coinbase premium 7-day average is −0.174%: the loss selling is spot, not leverage.
findings.alt: Oct 30's loss selling coincides with the Binance theft, and part may be internal moves by the exchange or affected users (per-UTXO data cannot separate transfers); the brief flags no transfer day today. CheckOnChain values are smoothed and about 1 day late, and the daily figure averages intraday capitulation with same-day profit taking. The 75,819 cost basis is bitcoin-data's Oct 24 value (about 6 days late); CheckOnChain's 75,064 uses a different method and is not subtracted. Modeled STH total differs from actual by +2.1%, with 11.0% misplaced.
findings.history: Last three STH-SOPR loss-selling lows: Jul 13 0.9762, Aug 1 0.9936, Aug 14 0.9946 (all near 62K); today's 0.9917 is deeper than the last two and shallower than Jul 13. 3 samples, background only. Similar 7-day drops in supply in profit occurred 8 times (since 2022-11), with a 30-day median of 0.0% vs a +2.3% baseline; the latest two, 2025-09-26 +1.8% and 2025-11-03 −12.1%, point different ways.
findings.so: Scenarios (conditional, CheckOnChain Oct 30): a close at 76,000 puts about 2.37M BTC of short-term supply at a paper loss (65%), 2.40M at 74,000, 2.51M at 66,000, only 140K more in between (thin), jumping to 2.93M at 64,000. Logic chain: last edition's '80–82K lost' has happened and new buyers are now selling at a loss, so the pressure moved from paper to realized; STH-SOPR is not yet deeper than Jul 13 and price is still above the short-term cost basis, so 'short-term capitulation' is not yet established. Market stage and exit framework are unchanged; the 200-day MA is 5.3% away.
findings.next: By Nov 6: short-term realized losses above 5,000 BTC would mean loss selling is widening (confirm); STH-SOPR back above 1.005 would mean it was a one- or two-day panic (refute).

findings.title: Longs rebuilt a day after the flush while the spot discount deepened
findings.lean_why: Spot is doing the selling while leverage was re-added at once: no buyer support underneath and a fresh pile of longs that can be liquidated.
findings.what: Weighted funding went from 0.64% (Oct 29) back to 9.85% (Oct 30), with Hyperliquid flipping from −8.54% to 10.95%; the same day CoinDesk counted $1.57B of 24-hour liquidations ($522M in BTC). Coinbase premium −0.243% on the day, 7-day average −0.174% (1-year percentile 0.3, lowest since the series began in 2026-01, n=299).
findings.why: Breakdown: which venue? The largest by open interest, Hyperliquid ($3.31B) and OKX ($2.70B), are both at 10.95%; only Deribit ($0.71B) fell to 0.52%. Deribit perp minus basis −5.02 points and median futures basis 5.54%: no panic discount in futures. Spot: the Coinbase discount to Binance has been beyond −0.24% for two days, and CoinDesk put the Coinbase premium z-score near −2, the deepest since the late-2025 sell-off. Cross-check: ETF Oct 29 provisional +$17M (about 88% below the prior day), stablecoins 7-day −1.17% (DefiLlama Oct 30): neither spot funding source filled the gap. Options: DVOL fell 41.99 → 40.59, and the risk reversal deepened only slightly to −5.03.
findings.alt: With Binance deposits and withdrawals paused, Binance BTC-USDT pricing may be distorted by blocked arbitrage, so part of the Coinbase premium may reflect the Binance side rather than US spot selling. Funding is a spot reading that swings intraday; Binance and Bybit funding are not available. Liquidation tallies use different windows (CoinDesk $1.57B, TokenPost $1.52B).
findings.history: The Coinbase premium 7-day average hit a 1-year 2% extreme only twice before (after 2026-06-02 the next 30 days were −7.7%; after 2026-06-28 +7.1%): too few samples, background only. We have no historical stats for funding jumping from near 0 to 10% in a day.
findings.so: This changes last edition's read that 'leveraged longs were largely flushed, leaving less room for liquidations to amplify the next drop': leverage is back and that cushion is gone. Unchanged: US spot remains a net seller, continuing 2026-10-29-2. Market stage and exit framework are unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 6: weighted funding below 3% would mean longs were flushed again or left, refuting 'leverage build-up'; for the Coinbase premium 7-day average below −0.2%, see 2026-10-29-2.

research.summary: Glassnode published Strategy Watch #9 on Oct 30 (an institutional monthly on September data) with no new price levels; its Oct 28 weekly call of 'thin demand' has played out, with price now near its 75.8K short-term holder cost basis.

items.title: Strategy Watch #9
items.points: September institutional flows: BTC 30-day net inflow peaked near $13.5B on Sep 22, then eased; US spot ETF 30-day inflow dipped to 13.7K BTC on Sep 20 and recovered to 34K BTC by month end, $2.65B for September; treasury companies returned as buyers; CME basis yield peaked Sep 19 and faded within ten days; manager cash 19.1% → 12.2%.
items.meaning: A September review, more than a month older than our readings; its question of whether inflows hold 'when the price stops helping' is exactly today's: our ETF 7-trading-day sum is down to +$202M and the Coinbase premium is at a low.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Quiet Under $85K
items.points: 84–85K has capped price four times this year; US spot ETF cost basis 81.5K, True Market Mean 77.9K, short-term holder cost basis 75.8K; conclusion: range-bound, thin demand but light sell pressure.
items.meaning: 'Light sell pressure' has been overturned by two down days and STH-SOPR below 1; price 77,204 is below its 77.9K True Market Mean and above its 75.8K short-term cost basis, nearly identical to our bitcoin-data 75,819.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 44
items.points: Failed push to 85K, back near 80K; futures open interest $37.5B with elevated long funding payments; spot CVD −$80.5M; conclusion: weak, defensive.
items.meaning: Negative spot CVD matches our Coinbase premium making new lows; the elevated long funding it flagged was liquidated on Oct 29 and was back at 9.85% on Oct 30. The next Market Pulse is expected Nov 1.
